newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Rules-North Melbourne end Sydney's AFL run.
newsitem.headline: Australian Rules-North Melbourne end Sydney's AFL run.

text.p: North Melbourne went on a second half goal spree in front of 93,102 fans at Melbourne Cricket Ground on Saturday to beat the Sydney Swans 19.17 (131) to 13.10 (88) in the Australian Football League (AFL) grand final.
North Melbourne's resounding victory denied Sydney their first AFL title after the Swans had topped the AFL regular season standings.
Sydney started the grand final at an exhilirating pace as forward Tony Lockett kicked three goals for the Swans to lead by 18 points at the end of the first quarter.
The Swans extended their lead to 24 early in the second quarter before North Melbourne began a match-turning fightback and kicked five goals to Sydney's two to lead by two points at halftime.

North Melbourne, representing the uniquely Australian game's heartland in the southern state of Victoria, then added another four goals in the third quarter to establish a comfortable 25-point buffer at three-quarter time.
Sydney tired visibly in the final 25-minute term after a tough finals series which included a one-point victory over Essendon in last Saturday's semifinals.
North Melbourne capitalised on Sydney's ragged defence to kick seven more goals in the final quarter to win by 43 points.

North Melbourne's previous AFL pennant win was in 1977. Sydney came into being in 1982 after the financially troubled South Melbourne club moved north to become the first AFL side based outside Victoria.
